features.cite: Zertal 1996 (Eng. Vol. 2) Site 148, p. 410; Fig. 326, p. 411
features.quote: 50 m north of the "Kurgan" ... large, empty burial cave
features.subtype: burial cave with steps leading into it

date.basis: not dated; the site's pottery (Chal-LB I) dates the site, not the cave

features.quote: To the north of the site there is also a hewn basin

notes: Entry grid 1893/1849 is the unit point exactly. The burial cave (f1) is placed 50 m north of the 'Kurgan', which is part 1 and the central part of the site. That is a reference point other than the site, so relative_to is other. On Fig. 326, cave no. 3 lies roughly N of the Kurgan, at about 55-60 m by the 25 m bar and the north arrow. This agrees with the text, but the unit point itself cannot be placed on the plan, so I used no plan position. The hewn basin (f2) has no size, so pool_def is unclear. It is probably the 'Installation' (Hebrew label: basin) at the north end of Fig. 326. The Kurgan (a mound of ash and burnt bones, read as a cultic fire-sacrifice site) and the tumuli are not called graves or burials by the entry, so they are not coded. 'Cisterns: none' is recorded as a C2 absence (cisterns only).
